nodes.summary: HAMPATH lies in NP, and every decision problem $L$ in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to HAMPATH: a polynomial-time computable map $f$ on bit strings such that, for every bit string $x$, $L$ accepts $x$ exactly when HAMPATH accepts $f(x)$.

nodes.summary: Let $x$ and $w$ be bit lists. Start the verifier at its start label, with either value of its Boolean variable, with $x$ on stack $\mathsf{X}$ and $w$ on stack $\mathsf{W}$ (as bit symbols, first bit on top) and all other stacks empty. Then within $100(|x| + |w| + 1)^4$ steps it reaches the label $\mathrm{yes}$ if the Hamiltonian path check accepts $x$ and $w$, and the label $\mathrm{no}$ otherwise.

not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.
